description:
Episode 37 of a daily journey through the universe. 👨‍🚀
We move into the International Space Station: home to people nonstop since 2000, 16 orbits a day, astronauts growing taller, 98% of water recycled (yes, including urine), and how to spot it from your backyard.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 38: Next stop, Apollo 11. The computer that took us to the Moon.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #spacestation #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Episode thirty-seven. Next stop... the International Space Station.
The International Space Station orbits about four hundred kilometers above us. People have lived on it nonstop since the year two thousand.
segments.headline: Home since 2000

segments.text: It circles the Earth about sixteen times a day.
In space, your spine stretches out. Astronauts can grow up to about five centimeters taller, then shrink back on Earth.
segments.headline: You grow taller

segments.text: About ninety-eight percent of its water, including sweat and urine, is recycled into drinking water.
It's about the size of a football field, and on a clear night you can see it pass over your house.
segments.headline: Visible from your backyard
